On point: Lutheran North keeps rolling up victories at fast pace on volleyball court
articles.content: When Macomb Lutheran North captured the Macomb BCD Tournament last weekend, it was another sign that the state-ranked Mustangs are for real. Off to the best start in school history – all for a program that was established back in the late 1970s – Lutheran North is 31-2-0 overall and how has an unbeaten record in the Blue Water Area Conference at 7-0. That included a five-set thriller win over state powerhouse North Branch – a program with multiple state championships and Final Four appearances – in the school’s very first BWAC game on Sept. 10. The team’s two losses have come against quality programs, including a three-set loss to Division 1 Port Huron Northern (19-4-0 overall) back on Aug. 25, while the Mustangs’ other setback came in a five-set thriller to Division 2 second-ranked Detroit Country Day on Oct. 15. “We were right there with Country Day, one of the best teams in the state, and lost that fifth set, 18-16,” noted Lutheran North coach Paul Drdul. “I knew we would have a good team this year. We have several girls that are in their third year (on varsity). But I wasn’t sure how we would do in the BWAC. Last year we were competitive in the Catholic League (AA Division) and lost in the conference tournament finals. At the Richmond-hosted BCD Tournament, Lutheran North continued its impressive season by going 6-0-0 to take home the title and jettison the team’s record to over on the day to win the BCD Tournament. The Mustangs defeated Warren Regina, Chesterfield Austin Catholic, Sterling Heights Parkway Christian, Armada, Richmond and New Haven to capture the tournament championship. Juliette Godwin led the Mustangs with an outstanding all-around performance, recording 25 aces, 66 assists and 18 digs. Godwin capped off her serving performance against New Haven by serving 25 consecutive serves in a perfect set to close out the game. That is one of the best single-set performances in school history. Eleanore Martin also had a strong day, finishing with 40 assists and 16 digs. The Mustangs’ offense was led by Lily Verbeke with 29 kills. Delaney Behring added 27 kills, 6-foot-2 Leighton Garner contributed 23 kills, while Lily Leinberger slammed 19 kills. Senior libero Victoria Burnham anchored the Mustangs’ defense with 46 digs and 42 receptions while also contributing 22 assists. Peyton Kraatz had 18 digs and 28 receptions. Sammy VanSteenkiste was also impressive by recording 10 kills, nine aces, 21 digs and 42 receptions. The overall balance – that’s what makes this team special, according to Drdul. “We don’t really have that one player. It’s always a total team effort,” said Drdul. “We have players that play their parts. It all starts with our setters, and then it leads to our middles and outside hitters. Defensively, we have done a great job on serve receive and keeping the ball in play. As a team, we serve (at a high clip).” Lutheran North will visit United Wholesale Mortgage in Pontiac, site of the annual BWAC league tournament which begins at 8:30 a.m. Saturday. The Mustangs, who currently have eight points atop the BWAC standings are the top seed of the eight-school tournament. “We’re in first place right now so we still have a chance at winning the (overall) league title,” said Drdul. “There’s a chance we could win this tournament which would give us the overall title. There’s also a possibility that we could see North Branch again.” Lutheran North celebrated Senior Night in style Wednesday evening, sweeping Almont in straight sets, 25-8, 25-12, 25-14. The Mustangs were led by their seniors, who made significant contributions on both sides of the net. Senior Victoria Burnham anchored the defense with 15 digs, 12 serve receptions, and four assists. Middle hitters Delaney Behring and Leighton Garner dominated at the net, with Behring recording seven kills on 11 attempts and Garner adding six kills on 10 attempts. Both middles also contributed three blocks apiece. Marian VanSteenkiste added five kills and two blocks. Lutheran North also received strong contributions from its underclassmen. Sophomore Juliette Godwin dished out 14 assists while adding three aces and six digs. Junior Lily Verbeke led the Mustangs’ offense with eight kills and added four aces from the service line. Junior Eleanore Martin contributed 10 assists, six digs, and one ace.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows New Hampshire to fully ban student IDs for voting in midterms
articles.description: Supreme Court allows New Hampshire to fully ban student IDs for voting in midterms AP News Supreme Court blocks use of student IDs as voter identification in New Hampshire Fox News Supreme Court sides with GOP in New Hampshire student ID voting fight Yahoo US Supreme Court allows N.H. to ignore student IDs for voting purposes in Nov. 3 election The Boston Globe Supreme Court Allows Blanket Ban on Student IDs at Polls
articles.content: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court cleared the way Thursday for New Hampshire to fully ban the use of student IDs for voting during the midterm elections. The justices granted a Republican-backed emergency appeal and blocked the use of student IDs as a backup method of identification. The Supreme Court cited a longstanding legal principle that judges shouldn’t change voting rules too close to Election Day. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only justice to publicly dissent. New Hampshire passed a law this year that said student IDs would no longer be an expressly accepted form of identification for obtaining a ballot. The secretary of state then issued guidance barring them as a backup way to prove a voter’s identity. A judge left the law in place but blocked the guidance in early October, prompting the appeal to the Supreme Court. The Republican National Committee weighed in to support the state. The decision comes less than two weeks before New Hampshire voters cast ballots in a closely contested U.S. Senate race. New Hampshire state Rep. Donald McFarlane said he sponsored the bill to eliminate student IDs for voting because colleges don’t have the same controls when issuing those cards as government agencies. “Today’s Supreme Court decision is a victory for common sense,” he said in an email. “It allows HB 323 to work as intended: strengthening voter identity verification, applying a consistent standard, and maintaining public confidence in New Hampshire elections.”

articles.title: El Salvador deploys special forces to Haiti to help find 4 missing soldiers who came under attack
articles.description: El Salvador deploys special forces to Haiti to help find 4 missing soldiers who came under attack AP News El Salvador sends troops to Haiti to rescue four service members CNN El Salvador's president threatens Haitian gangs over military hostages BBC El Salvador’s President Issues Harsh Warning to Haitian Gangs After 4 Soldiers Are Abducted The New York Times Bukele says military operation launched to rescue Salvadora
articles.content: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — El Salvador deployed 100 special forces soldiers to Haiti on Thursday to help rescue four missing soldiers from the Central American country who recently came under attack by gangs, two officials told The Associated Press. The special forces arrived a day after Salvadorean President Nayib Bukele announced a military operation to rescue the four aviation technicians and threatened a more forceful response if they’re not released alive and unharmed. An official with El Salvador’s government not authorized to speak on the matter said an additional 100 soldiers were going to be deployed to Haiti on Thursday night. The official said Salvadorean authorities were operating under the assumption that the four missing Salvadoreans are still alive. The Miami Herald first reported the deployment. The gang suppression force issued a brief statement late Thursday saying that “a contingent” from El Salvador had arrived “to support ongoing search and security operations” where the attack occurred. Haiti’s government said Wednesday evening that the four missing soldiers were abducted, marking its first comments since the attack that occurred Sunday in Croix-des-Bouquets. Authorities have said the soldiers were traveling in an armored vehicle that came under fire from gangs that also used explosives. It’s the first major attack since the international gang suppression force began operations, replacing a Kenyan-led force that struggled to help Haitian police quell gang violence given a lack of resources and funds. Diego Da Rin, an analyst with the International Crisis Group, said he believes that finding the Salvadoreans will be like finding a needle in a haystack. “It will be almost impossible to find them … unless the gangs agree to hand them over,” he said. Da Rin said the Salvadoreans were apparently not traveling with the type of security detail needed so deep in gang-held territory, and it’s not clear what they were doing in the area. The attack occurred in territory controlled by the Chèn Méchan gang, with the 400 Mawozo gang operating just west of that area, a gang that is much more powerful and has far greater firepower. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack, and neither gang has posted about it on social media. Da Rin said he believes the unaccounted for soldiers could serve as a negotiation tool for gangs. “The silence surrounding the situation of the Salvadorans might actually help them increase the leverage they can use to compel the authorities to enter into negotiations,” he said. “I do not believe this kidnapping is so much an attempt to gain money, but rather an effort to prevent incursions into their territories.” Authorities have been fighting armed men in the area ever since the attack occurred, with the Haitian National Police task force, which includes Vectus Global — the private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince — working with the gang suppression force as part of a joint operation. As the heavy fighting in deep, gang-controlled territory continues, residents have been warned to remain indoors. The attack occurred as the gang suppression force numbers only a little over 2,000 of the 5,500 personnel envisioned. “The (force) was not prepared to begin its offensive campaign against the gangs,” Da Rin said. “The risk of launching large-scale operations is that the gangs might rejoin forces… and launch coordinated attacks.” He noted that the force generally makes incursions and clears territory that would then be secured by Haitian forces: “Now, all forces are playing an offensive role.” On Wednesday night, a gang leader known as Krisla who controls an area that is not located near the site of the attack, posted a video in which he mentioned Bukele and the ongoing gunbattle. “They have bigger weapons and more technology than we do, but we’ll fight to the end,” he said. “We didn’t ask Bukele to come here, we didn’t ask Bukele to send soldiers here. Bukele has come here to protect his money at his soldiers’ expense.” Part of the contractors working with Prince’s Vectus Global are from El Salvador, Da Rin noted. El Salvador’s presidential office did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment. Janetsky reported from Phoenix, Arizona.

articles.title: Whitmer encourages Michiganders to vote early
articles.description: In light of a recent statement issued by the Michigan Attorney General’s office announcing plans by the U.S. Department of Justice to send DOJ election monitors to polling places in […]
articles.content: In light of a recent statement issued by the Michigan Attorney General’s office announcing plans by the U.S. Department of Justice to send DOJ election monitors to polling places in seven Michigan municipalities, Gov. Gretchen Whitmer is urging constituents to vote early. At the launch of gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson’s “Driving Down Costs” bus tour outside the Michigan Education Association headquarters in East Lansing, Whitmer addressed concerns about possible federal interference in the upcoming midterm election. “We will do everything we can to ensure that people have absolute confidence they will be safe to go to the polls,” she said to reporters. By casting a ballot early, voters can “avoid any shenanigans that the Trump administration may or may not explore undertaking as we get closer to this election.” A spokesperson for James said, in a statement: “While Jocelyn Benson is beholden to coastal elites and Big Tech billionaires, John James answers to the people of Michigan. Michiganders are fed up with Democrats in Lansing using political stunts to distract from their disastrous policies that have raised our costs, lost our jobs, and failed our kids. On November 3rd, Michiganders will hold them accountable and elect John James to turn our state around.” Benson and Whitmer were accompanied by Benson’s running mate Senate Majority Leader Winnie Brinks. Brinks broke records as the first female Senate Majority Leader, and the Benson-Brinks ticket is a first for the state’s major-party election history. The job now is to get voters to submit their ballots, Brinks said. “We know there are lots of Republicans and Independents out there who are dissatisfied with Trump and all of his cronies.” Lansing Mayor Andy Schor also attended the event and called the all-female ticket a strong team. “Jocelyn Benson has Winnie Brinks. Winnie Brinks has gotten the job done in our state senate.” “Her opponent has someone for lieutenant governor … I don’t even know his name.” Speakers at the kickoff, like MEA President Chandra Madafferi, highlighted the candidates’ links to public schools as a sign of loyalty to educators. The MEA officially endorsed Benson in Aug. just after the primary election. Both of Benson’s parents were public school teachers. Brinks was an educator in Grand Rapids Christian Schools and Godfrey-Lee public schools, according to the her biography in the Library of Michigan. Educators need better compensation and labor rights protection, and the Benson-Brinks ticket promises that, Madaferri said. State Rep. Penelope Tsernoglu, from the 75th District, highlighted successes of Brinks’s leadership in the state Senate, like repealing Right-to-Work laws and codifying reproductive rights in the state constitution and expanding protections for Michigan’s LGBQT+ community. “We’re looking to these strong, powerful women to bring us back into a trifecta, so we can get back to work for you and everyone in Michigan,” Tsernoglu said. In her speech, Benson urged the crowd to help push voter turnout. “Because whether it comes to education, creating well-paying jobs, ensuring we’re protecting labor and union rights, ensuring we’re protecting our kids,” she said, “it all comes down to what we do over these next 12 days.” Benson tied her opponent, U.S. Rep. John James, to higher costs to the policies pushed by President Trump. “[James] has already shown us who he is fighting for … Every lie Trump tells, he repeats,” she said. “Every bad economic policy, the war in Iran, driving up our health care costs, tariffs that are taxing basically everything we buy, he supports.” When it comes to the election, Benson called herself “an election defender,” even if it “means sheltering in my home in Detroit.” She was referring to an incident in Dec. 2020, when armed protesters who were upset about the results of the recent election descended on her home. Benson did not provide a firm answer when asked about working with President Trump on issues, instead telling reporters that she would “fight aggressively” to bring well-paying jobs to the state. “Let me also be clear. When or if he lies, if he tries to overturn our elections, if he tries to violate the law and send federal troops to terrorize our communities or interfere with our democracy, I will be there to stand in the way.”

Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear
articles.description: Warhound, the brainchild of Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, emerges from stealth to genetically engineer dogs for military and law enforcement.
articles.content: Colossal Biosciences’ Ben Lamm and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey had an idea to genetically engineer war dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement, and other emergency response teams. On Thursday, that idea came out of stealth as Warhound, backed by $200 million in funding from investors including Sequoia, 8VC, and In-Q-Tel, a venture firm backed by the CIA and other U.S. intelligence agencies. The round values the company at $1.2 billion. Warhound’s dogs, which do not exist yet, will take on tasks that are dangerous for humans or difficult for machines, such as bomb detection, searches, and other specialized operations. In its launch announcement, the company said that more than 80% of the U.S. military’s working dogs come from Europe, and less than half of them are fit for service. That means the supply of working dogs is dwindling, and the U.S. increasingly relies on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the military and in law enforcement. Warhound aims to change that. The hope is that Colossal can use its technology to engineer dogs with “characteristics suited to demanding missions,” the company said in a press release. Lamm told TechCrunch he met Luckey about a year ago at a conference, where Luckey said more should be done for the military’s working dogs. The two kept in touch, and Lamm researched how working dogs are bred. He learned that many of them do not make it through training because of inherited predispositions to problems like poor eyesight or the high possibilities of cancer, hip dysplasia, or muscle atrophy. Lamm believed dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity, and “for things like speed and agility or enhance olfactory sensors for bomb sniffing and whatnot,” he said. His team studied top-performing working dog breeds — the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd — taking cell lines (living cells grown in a lab) from them and putting them in a biobank. From there, the team will edit the dogs’ genes, adding ones that will improve performance and removing ones that will not, to create “a new type of dog.” Anduril, meanwhile, will provide software and hardware, such as protection vests and goggles, to assist the dogs and their handlers with situational awareness and coordination. Lamm said to imagine, for example, bulletproof vests with data sensors that send information back to the handlers so they can better understand what is happening. “The idea is, if we make the dog safer, make it healthier, make it perform better, it’s going to perform better in the line of duty,” Lamm said. He added that Anduril’s additions will make the dogs safer and healthier beyond their genetics, “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” He believes the enhancements will also better protect the dogs’ human handlers. Luckey is a partner in the venture but owns no equity in it, Lamm told TechCrunch. Colossal owns equity in the business and supports it by licensing its technology. Colossal is currently known for its de-extinction efforts to bring back animals like the dodo and the mammoth. As Lamm previously told TechCrunch, the company has been using AI, buying and building technology to help with gene cloning and with identifying and copying animal genes. Lamm said the first batch of dogs is about to be cloned and incubated, with births expected early next year and service ideally beginning within two years. Viagen, another Colossal-owned company, will partner with Warhound to clone the dogs. Lamm said Viagen’s technology has a high cloning success rate, and Colossal already uses it in its program to protect endangered species. Warhound doesn’t know yet how much it will charge for the dogs, but it expects to sell to first responders, the Department of Defense, military service groups, and police forces. Asked about government approval, Lamm said the company has briefed many government groups about the business. Asked about civilian safety once genetically enhanced dogs enter service, Lamm said each dog will be trained like any military working dog and managed by whoever buys it. The company said it is working under the guidance of the American Humane Society to help certify Warhound’s training program for the new dogs. The hope is also that when these new military dogs retire, they will enter the Society’s Military Working Dog Reunification Program, which provides homes for retired military dogs — or another program the Society offers to help dogs. articles.content: Demand for new PCs took a hit after months of price hikes, with Counterpoint Research reporting global PC shipments fell 21 percent year-over-year in Q3 2026. That’s in line with earlier reports from IDC and Omdia. It’s not just PCs, either — that same quarter, smartphone shipments also hit a 14-year low. Counterpoint linked the decline in PC shipments to higher component prices. Up until Q2 2026, PC shipments had been growing for over two years straight. But over the last several months, RAM, SSDs, and chips from Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm have all gotten more expensive, leading to price hikes on everything from MacBooks to Raspberry Pis. Counterpoint senior analyst Minsoo Kang noted that some companies are shifting to “prioritize configurations that can better absorb component inflation,” leaving fewer affordable options for price-sensitive buyers. Some companies are even reviving older tech, like DDR4 RAM and 4GB GPUs, to help mitigate price hikes. Counterpoint also says Q3 2025 included “purchases ahead of the Windows 10 support deadline and tariff-related inventory adjustments,” which added to the sharp year-over-year drop this past quarter. The PC market might not bounce back anytime soon, as Counterpoint associate director David Naranjo says, “With global shipments expected to plunge 27% in Q4 2026 and remain broadly flat in 2027, stabilization should not be mistaken for recovery.”

articles.title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
articles.description: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
articles.content: OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company. TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.” Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically. In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. Andrew Hsu, the CTO at Speak, which builds AI language tutors, said the Decisions API allowed the company to cut the time between actions from 1.4 seconds to .13 seconds. OpenAI also used the product to improve their Dots voice assistant’s responsiveness. Still, it’s not clear exactly what makes a good decision model, other than “it works for you” — optimization across intelligence, cost, calibration, and speed seems to differ by workload. TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida distrusts benchmarks and urges people to trial the models in their own work, but even TypeSafe released its own rankings last week alongside the release of its latest Jev model, which includes new features including support for images and smart-if statements. Public benchmarks like the AIM System One Index and the Artificial Analysis Decision Index tend to favor D1 Ultra, a new decision model that Liquid released last week, and Base Lab’s Elephant-1. The latest Jev model remains competitive on both indices, in seventh and third, with OpenAI’s Decision Model falling eighth and fourteenth, respectively. However, TypeSafe’s offerings are, for now, the most widely-queried on OpenRouter. The most fun Jev benchmark, however, is JevMan, a benchmark where decision models play PacMan; the latest Jev model tops that ranking. Felix Wunderlich, the chief growth officer at Opper AI, which built the benchmark, said the classic game “is an interesting test because of its nonstop stream of quick, high-stakes decisions. At every junction the model must decide where to go in a few hundred milliseconds.” Where OpenAI’s arguably more capable model may have an advantage is in multi-modality—for image classification, “Luna is extremely powerful and has been showing better calibrations,” Handa told TechCrunch, adding that OpenAI customers want the Decisions API to be more flexible about using images as outputs as well. Handa also saw further increases in speed enabling new use cases: “Can we get this to something like you know 60 milliseconds, and then you could imagine like an API like call like for every single frame in like a video?” As these offerings get faster and cheaper, we can expect them to live up to Jev’s namesake, an economist who explained how using a resource more efficiently makes it more ubiquitous. Or, as Handa sees it, there will be an expanding “crazy set of use cases” that were hiding in plain sight until the decision models revealed them. Trump’s math on US deal for Venezuelan oil doesn't add up, experts say. The bad data began years ago
articles.description: Trump’s math on US deal for Venezuelan oil doesn't add up, experts say. The bad data began years ago AP News What the U.S. Is Really Doing in Venezuela The Atlantic The secret terms of Trump’s Venezuelan oil deal Salon.com “A Coalition of Two Kleptocracies” Open Letters, from Anne Applebaum Venezuela claims to have 300 billion barrels of oil in the ground. But experts say that's a stretch Daily Gate City
articles.content: A single figure sets Venezuela apart from the rest of the world: 303 billion barrels of so-called proven oil reserves. But experts say the country’s estimate is inherently problematic and far from proven — rooted in exaggerated, aging data from a corrupt government. The number has long been touted by politicians and investors as an important measure of untapped energy potential, most recently by President Donald Trump’s administration in detailing a sweeping deal for the U.S. to take control of some Venezuelan reserves. But a more realistic estimate of the country’s proven reserves — a gold standard metric, representing the amount of oil that can reasonably be extracted under current conditions — is about one-third of what it has reported, half a dozen experts told The Associated Press. They put the likely figure at 60 to 120 billion barrels, a vast amount but not enough for Venezuela to remain the world’s largest holder of reserves. The distinction is an important one as Venezuela and the U.S. attempt to attract new investment into the country’s dilapidated oil industry, and it suggests that the deal Trump announced in August claiming the U.S. would ultimately control more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s proven oil reserves is much less profitable than he asserted. “That’s a funny, funny proposal,” Evanan Romero, a former Venezuela energy official now based in Houston, said of the deal, adding that he believes the Trump administration didn’t fully research the South American country’s claims before wading in. “If the U.S. government called them and asked them to testify to how they did the procedure — well, the whole world will know that that’s a funny number, an absolute lie.” Venezuela’s government didn’t respond to a request for comment from AP. Trump has said that under the deal, the U.S. will control 65 billion barrels of proven reserves — a figure exceeding the entirety of U.S. crude reserves. He’s repeatedly cited the 65 billion barrels number and called the oil deal the biggest in history, a way to refill U.S. strategic reserves and lower gas prices that surged during the Iran war. But experts say the U.S. is gaining access to a mix of sites that are nearly depleted or totally undeveloped, with an expected output a fraction of what Trump claimed. Some of the oil fields are deep within the Orinoco Belt, a virtual wilderness in central-eastern Venezuela posing major technical challenges. “We cannot believe the 65 billion. It’s impossible,” Romero said, adding that some firms have abandoned these fields because of the difficulties. The White House hasn’t publicly disclosed how it arrived at the 65 billion figure and didn’t answer questions from AP. A statement from White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers defended the deal and Trump’s assertions. “This historic deal marks a major step toward stabilizing Venezuela’s economy after years of hyperinflation and almost no new investment, while more than doubling the United States’ oil reserves,” Rogers said. Luisa Palacios, a former Citgo chair, said she suspects the figure announced by the administration represents oil stored underground, not proven reserves. Under that scenario, she said, the proven reserves would probably be about 10% to 12% of 65 billion, or around 6.5 billion. “Is that 65 billion barrels assuming a 20% recovery rate?” said Palacios, now an energy researcher at Columbia University. “That’s the thing that I cannot say. And so that’s why there are questions around it.” Francisco Monaldi, a Venezuelan oil expert at Rice University, estimated that 10 billion to 15 billion barrels would be classified as proven reserves in the short term — far short of Trump’s estimate. The oil the U.S. would control, according to officials in both countries, is in 17 fields under the control of a joint venture between the U.S. and Venezuela-based North American Blue Energy Partners, or NABEP. Publicly traded oil companies are required to report estimates of proven reserves in annual reports using strict definitions provided by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. NABEP isn’t publicly traded. The calculations behind Venezuela’s claim of more than 303 billion reserve barrels began over a decade ago. In the mid-2000s, then-President Hugo Chávez set out to tally reserves in the Orinoco Belt, amid increasing global oil prices and virtually unrestricted government spending. It became a multiyear effort, with state-owned companies from Brazil, Iran, China, Spain and other countries invited to help calculate the reserves, and a U.S.-based firm hired to study them. But the government never provided detailed explanations for the conclusions. Some experts and observers have questioned them since. “Those were funny numbers that were cooked by Hugo Chávez and his minister of energy at that time,” Romero said. Monaldi agreed: “They are inflated by a factor of nearly three.” The U.S.-based firm hired by Chávez estimated Venezuela had more than 1 trillion barrels of oil under the Orinoco Belt’s surface but never calculated its proven reserves, or the amount with a 90% chance of being extracted. Chávez’s government made that calculation itself. The firm, Ryder Scott, refused to sign off on the figure, ultimately abandoning its work, and didn’t provide comment to AP. In its 2011 annual report, Venezuela’s state-owned oil company said its proven reserves jumped by a stunning 82 billion barrels, to nearly 300 billion. The company — Petróleos de Venezuela S.A., or PDVSA — attributed it to “adjustments due to the revision of recovery” rates. PDVSA didn’t provide additional details; its operations, statistics and finances have been shrouded in secrecy for years. With that extraordinary jump, Venezuela surpassed Saudi Arabia as the world’s largest holder of proven reserves in OPEC’s annual reporting. Experts believe an accurate recovery rate for Venezuela’s oil reserves today is about 10% overall and even lower — 5% to 8% — in the Orinoco Belt, which has become an investment priority for acting President Delcy Rodríguez and the White House. The oil there is thicker than most conventional crude; it doesn’t easily flow into wells. Producers could use advanced technology to increase the recovery rate, but that requires major investments, which companies are hesitant to make in a country led by a government with a history of breaking contracts and current instability. Rodríguez’s term expired in July, and no elections are scheduled. OPEC has accepted the country’s proven reserves calculations and placed it atop the list of proven reserves every year since 2011. OPEC — comprising a dozen countries, with Venezuela as a founding member — didn’t respond to a request for comment. OPEC’s 2026 report sets Venezuela’s proven reserves at 303.7 billion barrels, which includes reserves in the Orinoco Belt and other oil-producing regions. Saudi Arabia ranked No. 2, with 267 billion barrels, followed by Iran, with 208 billion. Despite widespread skepticism, the 300 billion figure has stuck. Both Chávez’s successors — the now-deposed Nicolás Maduro and Rodríguez — have cited it repeatedly. So has the political opposition, including Nobel laureate María Corina Machado. The ruling party for 27 years also used the figure to secure multibillion-dollar loans from China and Russia. Experts said private investors considering Venezuela options will want to see accurate data from Rodríguez’s government. The lack of transparency, they said, only adds to investors’ hesitation. “Any country that reports a reserve figure that never changes over time — that smells extremely fishy,” Monaldi said.

articles.title: Voters prioritize costs and Iran over investigating Trump for next Congress, AP-NORC poll finds
articles.description: Voters prioritize costs and Iran over investigating Trump for next Congress, AP-NORC poll finds AP News Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey CNBC Trump’s approval rating flips with rural voters before midterms Yahoo Trump’s Repudiation Is at Hand, Right? The New Yorker Trump Approval Hits New Low Two Weeks Before Midterms, Poll Finds The New York Times
articles.content: WASHINGTON (AP) — Regardless of the outcome of the Nov. 3 election, a new AP-NORC poll shows voters from both major political parties want the next Congress to focus on making life more affordable and ending the war in Iran, while fewer are looking for an emphasis on President Donald Trump — whether it’s investigating him or supporting his agenda. The results suggest that voters are ready for Congress to tackle core issues, despite Trump’s centrality in the midterm campaign. About 8 in 10 registered voters, including a large majority of Republicans and Democrats, say lowering the cost of living should be one of the highest priorities for the session coming up, the survey from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research finds. Justin Campbell, a 31-year-old Democrat from Brookhaven, Mississippi, said he wants the government to focus on helping people like him rather than wealthy people. “I’m not a millionaire and probably won’t ever be,” he said. “I prefer policy that helps me instead of someone I’ll never be.” Most voters also want Congress to prioritize ending the war with Iran, with roughly 7 in 10 saying this should be a top focus. Substantially fewer voters, about 4 in 10, want Congress to make investigating the Trump administration a high priority, and only about 2 in 10 want Congress to prioritize supporting the Republican president’s agenda. But the poll also indicates that there are deep divisions within the parties on what to focus on, with moderate Democrats and Republicans differing sharply from voters on the left and right wings of their parties. Most Democratic voters who identify as supporters of democratic socialism are hoping for a Congress that will investigate the administration, and many want to end military aid to Israel, while MAGA Republicans are interested in Congress supporting Trump’s agenda. Moderates in both parties, are much likelier to want Democrats and Republicans to find common ground. Lowering the cost of living and ending the Iran war overshadow a wide range of other issues as voters consider priorities for the next Congress. While most registered voters say reducing costs and ending the war should be among the highest priorities for Congress, only about half say reducing the budget deficit and finding common ground between the two parties should be high priorities. About 4 in 10 want investigating the administration and passing new laws regulating artificial intelligence to be high priorities. Fewer, about 3 in 10, prioritize ending military aid to Israel, and only about 2 in 10 want a focus on supporting Trump’s agenda. The sun rises behind the Capitol Dome in Washington, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, two weeks before the midterm elections that will determine political control of Congress. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite) The sun rises behind the Capitol Dome in Washington, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, two weeks before the midterm elections that will determine political control of Congress. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite) Though most registered Democrats want Congress to investigate the administration, that falls behind the larger priorities of lowering costs and ending the conflict with Iran. About 6 in 10 registered voters who identify as Democrats call investigations into the administration “one of the highest priorities.” Arthur Brown, a 71-year-old Democrat in Magee, Mississippi, wants to see the next Congress work on making the economy stronger and prices lower. He feels less urgently about holding Trump accountable, mostly because there’ll be only two years left in Trump’s term. He thinks it’s more important to try to turn the economy around. “They should just focus on, you know, trying to tackle these problems,” he said. “Eventually down the road, justice will come.” For Republican voters, bolstering Trump’s goals also falls behind lowering the cost of living, ending the war in Iran and reducing the budget deficit. In a strikingly tepid show of support for the president, only about 4 in 10 Republican voters say the next Congress should make supporting the administration’s agenda one of its highest priorities. House Democrats have begun planning an ambitious 100-day agenda for what they would do if they win control of Congress in November. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York has said the party’s top priorities include making life more affordable and conducting vast oversight of the administration. But there are potential schisms in the party awaiting Democrats if they win a governing majority. The Democratic Party has reckoned in primary campaigns with a growing wing of democratic socialists. Their progressive stances on some issues have divided the party — including on whether to continue military aid to Israel, whether to compromise with Republicans and how strongly to investigate the administration. A sticker placed by an unidentified person depicting President Donald Trump and reading “I DID THAT!” is affixed beside gasoline and diesel prices at a gas station in Newtown, Pa., Sept. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Ted Shaffrey, file) A sticker placed by an unidentified person depicting President Donald Trump and reading “I DID THAT!” is affixed beside gasoline and diesel prices at a gas station in Newtown, Pa., Sept. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Ted Shaffrey, file) About three-quarters of Democratic voters who identify as supporters of democratic socialism say one of the top priorities should be investigating the administration, compared with slightly less than half of Democrats who say they’re not democratic socialists. Democratic socialists are also more likely to want Congress to end military aid to Israel and less likely to say it’s a top priority to find common ground between the two parties. Campbell, the Democrat in Mississippi, identifies as a democratic socialist and wants Congress to hold the administration accountable. “It feels a little cliche to just say roll back the past two years, but honestly, mostly just roll back the stuff he’s done the past two years,” Campbell said. Republicans are broadly aligned on what they want the next Congress to do, regardless of whether they identify with the “Make America Great Again” movement — except when it comes to Trump. At least half of MAGA and non-MAGA Republicans want leaders to lower costs, end the Iran war and reduce the federal budget deficit. Richard Longo, a 74-year-old Republican in Lake Forest, California, wants to see the president’s agenda pursued in the next Congress but is especially worried about balancing the budget. “You’re not going to balance the budget in one year, but you have to have a plan,” Longo said. But while about 6 in 10 MAGA Republicans want Congress to prioritize supporting the administration’s agenda, only about 2 in 10 Republicans who are not supporters of MAGA say the same. Lisa Ostlund, a 46-year-old from Wayland, Massachusetts, who identifies as a MAGA supporter, wants to see the next Congress prioritize Trump’s agenda. She doesn’t support everything Trump does, but she credits his policies with her recent ability to find housing after struggling with homelessness for several years. “You got to care about your American people,” Ostlund said. “He definitely doesn’t say it right, but you do have to put them first.” The AP-NORC poll of 1,119 adults was conducted Oct. 8-12 using a sample drawn from NORC’s probability-based AmeriSpeak Panel, which is designed to be representative of the U.S. population. The margin of sampling error for adults overall is plus or minus 3.9 percentage points.

Election 2026: Need special accommodations to vote? What you need to know.
articles.description: If you need special accommodations when you go to vote this Nov. 3, here's what you need to know.
articles.content: Q. How do I apply for an accessible absentee ballot? A. Voters with print disabilities may apply for an accessible electronic absentee voter ballot that can be completed electronically, printed, and returned to the local clerk. Q. How do I vote in person with an accessible voting machine? A. All voters, including voters with disabilities, have access to a Voter Assist Terminal in all polling places. The Voter Assist Terminal helps the voter mark a ballot. It will mark the ballot with the voter’s choices but does not tally the votes. Once the ballot is marked, it is counted in exactly the same fashion as all other ballots. A. Wayne County uses Liberty Vote. Click here to learn more about the system. Q. How can I prepare to use these machines? A. Michigan provides a YouTube playlist with videos detailing how to use the accessible voting machines. You can also contact your local election official for more information or assistance. Q. What to expect outside the polling place A. You have the right to an accessible polling place and an accessible voting machine. During the early voting period or on Election Day, you can send someone into the polling place to request curbside voting on your behalf. The election inspectors will bring a ballot outside so you can vote. Election officials must consider accessibility outside the polling place. You should expect: Q. What to expect inside the polling place A. You have the right to vote independently using an accessible voting machine. If you would like to use an accessible voting machine, tell an election official when you arrive to vote. You have the right to assistance from the election officials. You can ask the election officials for instructions on how to use the voting equipment or assistance at any time, even after you’ve entered the voting booth. If you are blind, disabled, or unable to read or write, you have the right to assistance from anyone you choose. However, the person cannot be: Election officials must consider accessibility inside the polling place. You should find: Q. What are my voting rights per state and federal law? The Voting Accessibility for the Elderly and Handicapped Act of 1984 (VAEHA) requires accessible polling places in federal elections for elderly individuals and people with disabilities. Where no accessible location is available to serve as a polling place, voters must be provided an alternate means of voting in person on Election Day. The Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA) requires at least one accessible voting system for persons with disabilities at each polling place in federal elections. The accessible voting system must provide the same opportunity for access and participation, including privacy and independence, that other voters receive. If you want to check that your polling location meets these standards or find an alternative polling location, contact your local election official. Q. What if I’m unable to stand long enough to wait in line? A. If you are unable to stand in line, you can request: If you do not read or write English and a ballot is not available in your language, you have the right to assistance from anyone you choose. However, the person cannot be: Q. Something went wrong? What can I do now? A. You can contact the Michigan Secretary of State by filling out an online form and selecting a reason for contact from the list. To speak with the Ombudsperson (person who handles complaints) for voters with disabilities, you can call 517-335-2730. You can email the Bureau of Elections at Elections@Michigan.gov if you believe that an election official has violated the Help America Vote Act. You can also fill out a Violation of Civil Rights Complaint Form and submit it to the US Department of Justice by one of the following methods: U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General Investigations Division ATTN: Civil Rights & Civil Liberties Complaints 950 Pennsylvania Ave., NW Washington, DC 20530 For additional assistance, The National Network of ADA Centers can provide local contact information for other organizations you may wish to contact, including your Regional ADA Center or ADA Knowledge Translation Center, or Federal Agencies and Resources. articles.title: CNN Live Event/Special
Mamdani has signed 1 law in 10 months — because his ‘obsessed’ staff is focused on ‘becoming a content farm’
articles.content: See more of our coverage in your search results. Mayor Zohran Mamdani has signed just one bill into law in 10 months since taking office — leaving critics to wonder if the millennial mayor is more interested in social media stardom than his daily government duties. Mamdani, who turned 35 on Sunday, signed a law allowing year-round outdoor dining on city sidewalks in August — and that’s the only City Council-passed bill he’s put his seal on so far while nearly 100 languish on his desk since January. Every other bill under the social media-savvy socialist’s administration has become law in a process known as “returned unsigned,” which automatically enacts a bill if the City Council passes it and it sits unsigned without a veto on the mayor’s desk for four weeks. Hizzoner, meanwhile, regularly appears in numerous cleverly crafted TikTok videos per day — prompting insiders to lament about where his priorities lie. “The mayor and his team are obsessed with becoming a content farm, often delaying or can-kicking boring governmental meetings so the mayor and his staff can hold pitch sessions for social media videos,” one source who often works with City Hall told The Post. “The mayor gets pitched comedy sketches more than Lorne Michaels,” the source added. “There are lots of laughs, and there is very little work.” Mamdani’s signature count is shockingly far behind his last three predecessors — former Mayor Eric Adams had signed 30 laws at the same point in his term, Bill de Blasio had signed 47, and Mike Bloomberg had signed 28. Although the “returned unsigned” route that’s dominated Mamdani’s term eventually nets laws, it’s far from normal — as mayors typically use it to protest legislation they don’t agree with, or to avoid being associated with an effort they know they won’t beat with a veto. But Mamdani doesn’t seem to have gotten that memo — as numerous bills he’s left unsigned play perfectly into his progressive agenda, including one overwhelmingly passed by the council that required ICE-barring sanctuary rules be posted at schools and city-owned buildings. It was introduced in February — a softball, two months into his term — but when the time came for him to sign the bill for socialist ally Alexa Aviles in June, the law was disregarded and left to languish for four weeks before automatically going into effect. That’s the playbook dozens of bills enacted during Mamdani’s administration have followed — all while he continues to personally appear in his social media clips, including two sketches Monday, two on Saturday and two on Thursday. Some of those social media hits have made huge headlines, even as valuable legislation sat waiting on his desk for his stamp of approval. That’s what was happening in July when Mamdani infamously called Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu a “war criminal” and said he’d looked into every avenue for New York City cops to arrest him. Bills awaiting his signature — and which never got them — when the video was released included one requiring wellness checks on elderly New Yorkers when temperatures rise above 95 degrees, one from a key Mamdani initiative expanding free childcare programs and one creating a rent-assistance program. Exactly why Mamdani is failing to sign bills of his own interest has left people even inside City Hall puzzled — while others have speculated his allies are probably shaking their heads. “It is a little bit weird. It gives the impression that enough attention is being paid or they disagree, but they don’t. I haven’t seen anything he’s disagreed,” former City Council member Diana Ayala said. “Those are his initiatives. “It would be nice to elevate their initiatives,” she said of council members whose bills Mamdani has neglected. “It shows goodwill and that they are in alignment on specific issues.” Others suggested Mamdani’s snubs were obvious — saying he prefers flashy executive orders and visuals that will play well on social media. “It’s easier to govern by TikTok than to actually perform the duties of the job,” a former City Hall staffer said. “They haven’t found a way to make this into compelling social media content,” added a former Bloomberg staffer. Another City Hall insider called the behavior “lazy government.” “It’s lazy in two ways — one is you are not taking a stand, easier to do nothing than figure out where you stand on something,” they said. “And lazy from a practical perspective — you can’t focus City Hall staff to hold the hearings, write the briefings and execute the bill signings.” City Hall did not respond to a request for comment.
